jobs.title: Finance Manager, Sales
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next.​

OVERVIEW

The Manager, Finance – Sales position at General Mills Canada Corporation is accountable for the financial management, oversight and partnership for a division of Customer Teams.

This role acts as a co-pilot for Sales Directors. The role requires holistic P&L Management & Performance while championing sustainable-profitable-growth and win-win retailer partnerships through short- and long-term mindsets. The role as co-pilot requires agility and strong prioritization, managing IBP/PEAK cycle cadence while providing thought leadership to help execute strategic plans. The right candidate will build a holistic understanding of internal & external P&L performance with an emphasis on the effectiveness of volume/mix choices and trade investments to support health of the business. The role offers great development opportunities for career growth, manages direct report(s) and reports to the Finance Director, Sales & Market Strategy & Commercial Capabilities.

Role Accountabilities:
- Responsible for partnering to lead Monthly Business Reviews to Review the Financial Forecast, Key External Leading & Lagging Indicators, an Actionable R&O as well as influencing key business hot topics requiring discussion to address R&O Items.
- Ability to proactively set priorities for self & team while remaining agile in an executional environment to ensure S&OP processes are adhered to while creating space for ad hoc projects while instilling a forward-looking mindset for the total team objectives.
- Champions strong controls across the Sales environment while overseeing monthly Trade Reviews to ensure strong forecast accuracy and effective trade investment.
- Practices strong communication and partnerships within broader Sales finance organization as well as MSRM finance group to ensure consistency across common priorities & objectives while continuously improving consistency through standardization initiatives.
- As a co-pilot to their Customer Team(s), operate as the financial leader to inspire broader sales teams in team townhalls to support delivering common objectives.
- Manage & coach direct report(s) for strong performance results and individual career development.

Professional Requirements and Experience:
- A university degree in Finance or Business Administration
- 5+ years of relevant experience in Finance, preferably in CPG
- Prior experience partnering with Sales Teams or externally facing roles Preferred.
- Agile, organized, and able to manage and prioritize changing workload for self & teams.
- Proven ability to build trusting relationships at all levels and across all functions; ability to effectively communicate and influence all levels across the organization.
- Strong track record of operating with gold-standard finance partnerships with an ability to influence senior leaders on the direction of the business.
- The ability to synthesize complex matters into simple and attainable solutions.
- Experience in a dynamic commercial facing role, with in-depth knowledge of inflationary and market pricing environment.

Leadership Competencies:

Business Partnership: Leads the business team in identifying and pursuing opportunities that maximize shareholder value; influences across boundaries to develop and execute long term strategies; drives sound/financial business decisions that balance internal P&L performance while remaining competitively externally.
Business Process and Analytics : Develops value-added insights, processes, reporting and analysis that drive business results; proficient in General Mills systems.
Technical/Financial Acumen: Demonstrates technical/financial knowledge in a value-added way; understands, practices, and propagates proper accounting, policy compliance and reporting while ensuring a strong control environment.

Ability to Create Flexible Environment: Ability to lead through ambiguity with agility in a dynamic and complex environment to support effective ways of delivering goals for the team.

Energizes and Develops People : Inspires and motivates, collaborates across boundaries, develops people, leverages teamwork, core strengths and diversity.

Delivers Outstanding Results: sets aggressive goals and priorities, delivers on short and long-term commitments, makes timely high-quality decisions, adds superior expertise.

Integrity: Engenders trust and credibility at all levels, demonstrates unquestionable integrity, and communicates openly and directly.

Additional Considerations:
- This role is based out of Mississauga, Ontario
- The posting for this position is to fill an existing vacancy within the organization.
- Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis.  General Mills will not sponsor applicants for this position for work visas.

General Mills is committed to Employment Equity and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates with disabilities taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process.

SALARY RANGE
The salary range for this position is:
$98,500 - $147,900 Annual

At General Mills we strive for each employee's pay at any point in their career to reflect their experiences, performance, and skills for their current role. The salary range for this role represents the numerous factors considered in the hiring decisions including, but not limited to expertise, skills, and relevant work experience. As such, pay for the successful candidate(s) could fall anywhere within the stated range.​
​

jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next.​

OVERVIEW
General Mills Treasury is seeking a highly motivated treasury professional for the role of Senior Treasury Analyst, North America Treasury Operations. At General Mills, the Treasury team creates shareholder value by optimizing GMI’s capital structure while flawlessly executing its fiduciary responsibilities. This includes efficiently managing cash flows, managing interest rate and foreign exchange risk, and protecting GMI’s financial assets. Treasury roles are highly technical and build strong knowledge of financial markets and cash management.

The Senior Treasury Analyst plays a key role supporting the function by securing capital to fund business operations, executing on cash management activities, handling bank relationships and monitoring financial risks for the North America region. This role also supports strategic corporate projects and partners with our treasury centers across the globe.

In this role, you will gain extensive experience in treasury operations and broad exposure to external banking partners and financial markets. This role builds functional experience in forecasting cash flows, issuing debt, managing derivatives, and supporting critical corporate initiatives such as M&A.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
- Manage the daily funding of bank accounts, including issuing Commercial Paper and investing excess cash to maximize returns while maintaining liquidity
- Build and maintain a long-term cash forecasts with inputs from various sources
- Remediate failed payments and fraud attempts
- Own the compliance and testing of SOX controls related to debt covenants, banking websites and cash movement
- Independently lead initiatives in a fast-paced environment
- Contribute to Treasury optimization through process improvements and automation
- Liaise with banks for operational services, including administrative oversight of bank accounts
- Partner with international treasury teams and domestic business partners to execute on high-profile initiatives, including bond offerings, share repurchases, legal restructuring, system upgrades, and M&A activity

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
- B.S. or B.A. degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or related field
- Minimum 3 years of relevant finance or operations experience
- Basic understanding of cash management, banking, debt instruments and derivatives
- Strong analytical skills, including a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail
- Ability to summarize complex concepts and build management-level reporting
- Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
- Exhibited a high degree of situational agility and change management
- Ability to independently manage multiple projects and prioritize effectively

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Treasury operations, cash management or cash forecasting experience
- SAP experience
- CTP or CFA

ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS
- Located at World Headquarters just outside Minneapolis, MN

- International relocation or international remote working arrangements (outside of the US) will not be considered.

- Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. General Mills will not sponsor applicants for this position for work visas.

SALARY RANGE

$82,400 - $123,800 Annual

The salary range for this role represents the numerous factors considered in the hiring decisions including, but not limited to, educations, skills, work experience, certifications, etc. As such, pay for the successful candidate(s) could fall anywhere within the stated range. ​

Beyond base salary, General Mills offers a competitive Total Rewards package focusing on your overall well-being. We are proud to offer a foundation of health benefits, retirement and financial wellbeing, time off programs, wellbeing support and perks. Benefits may vary by role, country, region, union status, and other employment status factors. You may also be eligible to participate in an annual incentive program. jobs.title: Brand Finance Manager, Responsable Financier des Marques, France Espagne, CDD, F/H
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next.​

Description du poste
Au sein de la Direction Financière de General Mills France & Iberia, le/la Brands Finance Manager France & Iberia est rattaché(e) au Finance Director FRIB et agit comme partenaire financier stratégique des équipes Brands (MATs) et Marketing sur le périmètre France et Iberia.

Le poste a pour mission de piloter l’agenda finance des marques Häagen-Dazs (HD), Old El Paso (OEP) et Nature Valley (NV), en accompagnant la performance des activités, les choix d’investissements et les décisions business au quotidien.

Le/la titulaire est également responsable de l’élaboration du budget des marques, également appelé Spring Plan (SP), ainsi que du plan stratégique à 3 ans (3OP), en collaboration étroite avec les Market Acceleration Teams (MATs) et les principales parties prenantes Finance et business.

Ce rôle combine business partnering, pilotage de la performance, planification financière et management d’équipe, avec une forte exposition aux enjeux de croissance, de rentabilité et d’allocation des ressources sur les marchés France et Iberia.

Missions principales
- Être le/la partenaire Finance de référence des équipes Brands et Marketing sur le périmètre France et Iberia, en apportant des analyses structurées et des recommandations actionnables.
- Piloter la performance financière des marques Häagen-Dazs (HD), Old El Paso (OEP) et Nature Valley (NV), en assurant le suivi du P&L, l’évaluation des initiatives et la priorisation des investissements.
- Encadrer, animer et développer l’équipe Brands Finance, en assurant un haut niveau d’exigence, de collaboration et de montée en compétences.
- Consolider et challenger les hypothèses financières des marques en lien avec les équipes cross-fonctionnelles et les Market Acceleration Teams (MATs).
- Piloter l’élaboration du budget des marques (Spring Plan / SP) pour la France et l’Iberia, en garantissant la cohérence des hypothèses, la qualité des analyses et l’alignement avec les priorités business.
- Coordonner la construction du plan stratégique à 3 ans (3OP) des marques en collaboration avec les MATs, en apportant une vision financière claire sur les trajectoires de croissance, de marge et d’investissement.
- Assurer le pilotage des dépenses Marketing et veiller à la bonne allocation des ressources au regard des priorités des marques et des objectifs financiers.
- Contribuer aux clôtures mensuelles, prévisions et exercices de latest estimate afin de garantir une vision fiable et à jour de la performance.
- Identifier les risques et opportunités, recommander des plans d’action et suivre leur mise en œuvre avec les équipes concernées.
- Préparer et présenter les analyses financières, scénarios et recommandations au management et aux parties prenantes clés.
- Faire progresser les outils, reportings et processus de pilotage afin d’améliorer la qualité, la rapidité et la pertinence des analyses.

Profil recherché
- Bac+5 école de commerce, Master Finance, Contrôle de gestion ou équivalent.
- Expérience significative en finance, contrôle de gestion, commercial finance ou FP&A, idéalement dans un environnement FMCG ou retail.
- Expérience confirmée de business partnering avec des équipes marketing, commerciales ou cross-fonctionnelles.
- Capacité démontrée à piloter des exercices de planification financière complexes tels que budget, forecast et plan stratégique.
- Très solides capacités analytiques, esprit de synthèse et aptitude à transformer les données en recommandations business.
- Expérience en management ou en coordination transverse fortement appréciée.
- Excellente communication, capacité d’influence et aisance dans un environnement matriciel et international.
- Français et anglais courants indispensables ; l’espagnol constitue un atout.
- Excellente maîtrise d’Excel et bonne connaissance des outils financiers ; une expérience sur SAP et des outils de reporting ou planification constitue un plus.
- Curiosité, leadership, sens du résultat et forte orientation amélioration continue.

Finalité du poste
Le/la Brands Finance Manager France & Iberia pilote l’agenda financier des marques Häagen-Dazs (HD), Old El Paso (OEP) et Nature Valley (NV), tout en assurant le suivi des dépenses Marketing et la qualité des décisions d’investissement. Le poste joue un rôle central dans la construction du Spring Plan (SP) et du 3OP des marques avec les Market Acceleration Teams (MATs), dans l’analyse de la performance et dans l’animation d’une équipe finance capable d’accompagner durablement la croissance rentable des activités sur la France et l’Iberia.

SALARY RANGE
The salary range for this position is:
€50,900 - €76,500 Annual

As such, pay for the successful candidate(s) could fall anywhere within the stated range.​
​

jobs.title: Operations Manager - Food Manufacturing
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next.​

About the Role
The Operations Manager owns production operations at the Pet Treating facility in Joplin, Missouri. Reporting to the Plant Manager, you’ll lead three supervisors and their hourly teams to deliver safe, high-quality products on time and within budget.

This role combines people leadership, production execution, food safety and quality, financial management, equipment reliability, and continuous improvement. You’ll develop frontline leaders, set clear performance expectations, use data to prioritize action, and lead improvements that strengthen safety, service, productivity, and cost performance.

What You’ll Do
- Lead daily production through three supervisor direct reports and their hourly teams.
- Set priorities, coach leaders, document performance, and hold employees accountable while maintaining trust.
- Build team capability through onboarding, job-transfer training, corrective and preventive actions, and ongoing development.
- Plan production to meet volume, efficiency, service, safety, quality, and cost objectives.
- Review daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs; identify trends; and convert findings into focused improvement plans.
- Lead practical lean initiatives, including Kaizen events, loss analysis, spaghetti diagrams, SMED, standard work, and visual management.
- Establish and sustain Operations-owned Autonomous Maintenance routines, including basic-condition restoration, cleaning, tightening, lubrication checks, and early identification of equipment abnormalities.
- Partner with Maintenance on equipment conditions and significant breakdowns while maintaining clear ownership of routine operator care.
- Use Redzone or a similar system to identify top losses, track actions, and improve equipment performance.
- Partner with Engineering to identify productivity opportunities, capacity constraints, and potential capital investments.
- Conduct or support facility capacity analysis and use the results to guide production planning and improvement priorities.
- Review existing bills of material for accuracy and partner with Finance on BOMs for new products after production trials.
- Analyze yield, waste, labor, downtime, and other cost drivers; then implement plans to improve performance.
- Own the department’s operating expenses, support annual budget planning, monitor results, and partner with Accounting on reviews.
- Partner with Quality to maintain product quality, food safety, and regulatory compliance, including FDA, FSIS, SQF, USDA, and GMP requirements.
- Champion a strong safety, food-safety, and quality culture through training, communication, audit follow-up, and procedural updates.
- Prepare operational reports, track issues and actions, and collaborate with Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Finance, and other support teams.
- Cross-train to provide manufacturing continuity and assume applicable Quality Assurance responsibilities when needed.
- Complete other assigned projects and responsibilities.

Minimum Qualifications
- Associate's or Bachelor’s degree in business administration, operations, manufacturing, or a related field is preferred.
- 5+ years of progressively responsible manufacturing experience, including experience in the food industry.
- 1+ year of experience directly managing salaried employees.
- Experience leading production or operations teams with responsibility for safety, quality, service, productivity, and cost.
- Experience leading or facilitating Kaizen events or other hands-on continuous improvement work.
- Working knowledge of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a production environment.
- Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to develop teams, set expectations, and hold people accountable without damaging trust.
- Experience managing operating expenses, developing budgets, and reviewing performance against plan.
- Knowledge of project management principles and practices.
- Ability to analyze operational data and prepare reports for reviews and issue tracking.
- Ability to work in hot, cold, or wet conditions, including temperatures below 50°F or above 90°F for periods of up to three hours.
- Ability to follow safety and PPE requirements when working with harsh cleaning chemicals.
- Ability to occasionally lift or move up to 50 pounds and work at elevation, including on a ladder, lift box, or scissor lift.

Preferred Qualifications
- Food manufacturing leadership experience in a regulated production environment.
- Experience managing multiple people leaders and hourly teams.
- Hands-on Autonomous Maintenance experience, including restoring equipment to basic condition and establishing operator-owned routines.
- Experience with Redzone or a similar digital production or loss-management system.
- Formal training in lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, Kaizen, or Total Productive Maintenance.
- Practical use of spaghetti diagrams, SMED, 5G/5S, standard work, loss analysis, and visual management.
- Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt training paired with practical application.
- Training Within Industry (TWI) experience, especially in standardized work, employee training, and change management.
- Experience analyzing capacity, equipment losses, yields, waste, labor, and other operating constraints.
- Experience reviewing or creating bills of material.
- Experience partnering with Engineering on productivity improvements and capital expenditure opportunities.

Additional Considerations

- Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. General Mills will not sponsor applicants for this position for work visas.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Operations Manager, South East Asia and Japan
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next.​

Role Overview
Supply Chain Operations Manager, SEA & JP leads CPFR (Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment) process with distributor partners across South-East Asia and Japan cluster. The role focuses on establishing reliable distributor data flows and actionable performance metrics, and ensuring demand visibility, product availability, inventory health and supply reliability by connecting distributor plans with General Mills commercial and supply chain processes.

The role partners closely with General Mills teams (Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Customer Service & Logistics, Supply Planning, Commercial, Finance, Marketing, COE and Global Business Support) and distributor supply chain and commercial teams. The CPFR Manager establishes a consistent operating rhythm, recurring planning and review routines, ensures high quality collaborative plans with distributors, improves alignment between General Mills and distributors on IMS, shipment, inventory and replenishment plans along with KPI’s and drives timely action on risks and opportunities.

Job Description
1. Distributor Collaboration and CPFR Governance
• Own the CPFR process and operating model for the assigned distributor markets & cluster
• Establish clear ways of working, meeting cadence, roles, decision rights, inputs, outputs and escalation paths
• Build trusted working relationships with distributor supply chain, commercial, customer service and logistics counterparts
• Lead regular joint planning reviews and ensure required inputs, decisions and actions are clear and timely
• Support distributor partners and planning teams on CPFR principles, forecast quality, inventory management including data requirements, ways of working, GMI processes and order placement timelines and performance tracking
• Build distributor planning maturity through standardized routines, data, performance management and joint accountability
• Ensure the distributor forecast collection, challenge and consensus process at the appropriate market, brand, SKU and time-horizon level
• Ensure distributor demand signals are mapped with commercial plans, promotions, launches, seasonality, market intelligence and historical consumption. Ensure commercial events, launches, portfolio changes and market risks are reflected in the planning cycle
• Drive distributor adherence to agreed order placement timelines per brands/plants
• Monitor distributor inventory (on hand and in transit), stock cover, open orders, and projected availability and ensure they are rightfully reflected in all relevant GMI tools
• Monitor actual sales, stock, shipments, orders, and forecast changes to identify risks and opportunities early
• Define and maintain replenishment parameters in partnership with distributors and internal planning teams
• Provide clear inputs to market or cluster S&OP forums and other business decision forums

2. Business Outlook, Service, Inventory and Supply Risks Management
• Ensure a high quality 12-month rolling IMS outlook to be built with the distributors with identified and actioned risks and opportunities
• Collaborate with demand planning team to identify and improve forecast gaps, demand volatility, supply-demand imbalances and projected service risks • Coordinate recovery plans for stock-outs, excess inventory, slow-moving or aged stock, supply constraints, expedites and order changes
• Escalate risks with the business impact, recommended action, decision owner and timing • Ensure order stability and reduce avoidable expedites, delays, cancellations, stock-outs and inventory build-up
• Support scenario planning and quantify the implications of key assumptions, risks and decisions

3. Performance Management, Analytics and Continuous Improvement
• Define and maintain dashboards covering forecast accuracy, forecast bias, primary and secondary service levels, stock-outs, stock cover, inventory health, order adherence and action closure
• Establish performance baselines and targets for each distributor
• Analyze trends and root causes of forecast error, service failures, inventory imbalances and planning instability and lead corrective actions with the appropriate internal and external stakeholders
• Improve and standardize data quality, master data discipline, reporting automation and planning transparency
• Measure the impact of improvements on service, inventory, cost, planning stability and distributor collaboration

4. Cross-Functional Leadership and Business Integration
• Influence internal and external stakeholders without relying solely on direct authority
• Lead through influence across a matrix of distributors and General Mills stakeholders
• Share best practices across markets and contribute to capability building within the distributor-market supply chain organization
• Demonstrate General Mills leadership behaviors by acting with pace, prioritizing what matters, winning as one team and doing the right thing, all the time

Key Performance Indicators
• Distributors forecast accuracy and forecast bias (M-3)
• Case-fill rate, primary and secondary service level, availability and stock-out rate
• Inventory coverage by distributor and category
• Order adherence, order stability and schedule change frequency
• CPFR action closure and process compliance
• CPFR maturity rating per distributor

Qualifications, Skills & Experience
1. Education
• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Economics or a related field
• Master’s degree or APICS/IBF certification is a plus

2. Experience
• 3-5 years of experience in demand planning, supply planning, customer collaboration, replenishment, logistics or end-to-end supply chain
• Proven experience working with distributor-led markets or distributors managing CPFR or planning processes across multiple geographies
• Practical experience with CPFR, S&OP / IBP, forecasting, inventory management and exception-based planning
• Experience leading cross-functional projects and influencing stakeholders without direct authority
• Experience in fast-moving consumer goods or a similarly demand-volatile, multi-SKU environment is preferred

3. Skills
• Define and maintain dashboards covering forecast accuracy, forecast bias, primary and secondary service levels, stock-outs, stock cover, inventory health, order adherence and action closure.
• Strong analytical and numerical ability, proficiency in Excel and planning tools (SAP APO/IBP, OMP)
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across functions and regions with effective negotiation skills
• A proven “doer” who acts with speed and agility to deliver results
• Deep understanding of forecasting methodologies, in market, shipment and inventory dynamics and S&OP processes
• Attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and ability to work in a dynamic environment
• Fluency in English

ELIGIBILITY
Applicants must meet minimum age qualifications in the country in which the job is located.
